You asked for a simple study that continuously records steps and tracks participants' locations hourly using their smartphones. Here’s what was built:

Participants will provide their full name during onboarding. Throughout the study, their smartphones will passively track and record step events continuously in the background. Additionally, the smartphones will collect hourly location data without requiring any active input from the participants.

We assumed that no other onboarding data is needed beyond the participant's full name. There are no open questions left to address.

Participants will record their step events passively through the smartphone without any action required from them. This happens continuously in the background. Additionally, the smartphone will sample the user's location once every hour, also in the background.

We assumed that the location service is properly connected to the smartphone for this study to function as intended. There are no open questions at this time.

We assumed that participants will provide their full names as required and that the smartphone will be used to sense step events. There are no open questions remaining.

You asked for a study to collect step events from a smartphone and location data from a connected service over a specified period. Here’s what was built:

You asked to create a mobile health sensing study that collects a variety of health metrics and user feedback using a smartphone. Here’s what was built:

Participants will provide essential information like birth date, gender, weight, BMI, and health metrics such as steps, heart rate, and sleep stages during onboarding. While the study runs, the smartphone collects data continuously on steps, location, battery status, screen status, ambient light, activity, connectivity, Bluetooth status, and WiFi status. Additionally, it records weather and air quality every 30 minutes and health data every hour.

Towards the end of the study, participants can submit feedback images on demand. We assumed that the health metrics and active task data will be kept even after being uploaded. There are no open questions at this time. However, it’s important to note that there were technical issues regarding the naming of some tasks that prevented certain uploads from being created, which we still need to resolve.

You asked for a study that collects health and environmental data through participants’ smartphones, including both passive data and periodic user-generated content. Here’s what was built:

Participants will provide their birth date and gender during onboarding. The smartphone will continuously collect data on steps, location, battery status, screen status, ambient light, activity, device information, connectivity, wifi status, and bluetooth status. Additionally, it will gather weather and air quality information every 30 minutes.

Every hour, participants will actively report their weight, BMI, steps, heart rate, and heart rate variability measures, as well as their sleep stages. Participants can upload pictures of their best demo or gadget on demand. 

We assumed that the app tasks will remain active throughout the study and that uploaded data will be retained locally. There are no open questions at this time.

You asked for a protocol to monitor participants' health metrics using a smartphone through both passive and periodic data collection. Here’s what was built:

At the beginning of the study, participants will provide their weight, BMI, birth date, and gender. Throughout the study, the smartphone will continuously collect data on steps, location, battery status, screen status, ambient light, activity level, device information, connectivity status, Wi-Fi status, Bluetooth status, weather, air quality, heart rate, and sleep stages, with some measures taken every hour and others every 30 minutes.

Participants can also upload images of their favorite demo or gadget whenever they choose during the study. We assumed that the data collected will remain on the device even after uploading, and that each image upload task will take about three minutes to complete. However, we still need to confirm the specific settings for data retention after upload and how to handle potential interruptions during these image upload tasks.

You asked for a mobile health tracking study that quietly gathers health and device metrics in the background, while also collecting weather and air quality data regularly and engaging participants with image tasks. Here's what was built:

The study collects various data from the participant's smartphone continuously, including steps, location, battery status, screen status, ambient light, activity type, device and network information, and nearby Bluetooth devices. It also gathers weather and air quality data every 30 minutes. Participants will actively provide their weight, BMI, date of birth, gender, heart rate, and sleep stages every hour. Additionally, they can take part in on-demand image tasks to upload pictures related to their favorite demo and gadget.

We assumed that the data is stored on the phone after uploading and that all data from the health app is available continuously. However, we still need to confirm what specific devices or services will collect the environmental data and whether there is a defined method for participants to report their health app data, as well as any specific parameters for the image tasks.

You asked for a study that silently monitors various health-related metrics and environmental conditions while allowing participants to engage in image-based assessments when they choose. Here is what was built:

The study actively collects data from the participant's smartphone continuously on steps, location, battery status, screen status, ambient light, activity, device information, network status, and nearby Bluetooth devices. You asked to create a study protocol that collects health and environmental data using mobile devices. Here’s what was built:

Participants will start with informed consent. Throughout the study, the smartphone will continuously gather a variety of data like location, screen activity, and ambient light. Weather and air quality information will be collected every 30 minutes, while health metrics will be recorded hourly.

You asked for a mobile health sensing study that collects health and environmental data through a Smartphone, along with user-uploaded photos of demos and gadgets. Here is what was built:

We assumed that the onboarding data will only include the wearable setup picture as specified. However, we still need to confirm details regarding notification times for image tasks, the specifications for health data from the online service, and how user engagement will be tracked for the health tasks.

You asked for a study to monitor and collect various health and wellness metrics using smartphone and wearable devices. Here is what was built:

You asked to onboard participants with their full name and to collect two data streams: continuous step events on the phone and hourly location samples, all uploaded in real time to the backend. The built setup matches this: the participant’s name is collected at the start, steps are recorded in the phone’s background, and location samples are gathered hourly, with data sent to the backend as a streaming feed. The location data comes from a Location Service bound to the phone.

How it works in practice:
- Location sampling: a Location Task runs in the background and is started in two ways. First, it begins immediately when the study starts (so you get an initial sample at deployment). Second, it runs hourly every hour. The Location binding uses high accuracy with a 10-meter distance filter and a roughly 1-minute internal update interval. You can see two active bindings for this task: one for immediate start and one for hourly sampling.
- Step events: a separate background task continuously records step events on the smartphone.
- Data destination: all data is uploaded in streaming fashion to the backend.

What this means for you: the setup fulfills your intent with immediate and ongoing location sampling plus continuous steps, plus full-name onboarding and streaming uploads. If you want a simpler behavior, we can keep only the hourly location sampling and remove the immediate startup binding, or vice versa. Open questions are resolved (first sample at deployment is enabled; both bindings exist and are active; no blockers). If you’d like, I can draft a deployment test plan to verify the startup and hourly sampling in a live run.

You asked for a study where the participant’s full name is collected at onboarding, the phone gathers steps continuously and location every hour, and all data are streamed to the CARP backend. The built protocol matches this plan in key ways.

What’s in the build
- Onboarding requires the participant to provide their full name.
- The smartphone is the main device used for data collection, and data collection starts automatically on the phone at the study start.
- The protocol sets up data collection on the phone to gather steps and location data, with the intent that steps are continuous and location is hourly (the cadence is described in your intent, but the protocol file does not spell out those exact intervals in detail).
- Data is sent to the CARP backend in streaming mode, with compression enabled, and it is allowed to upload over any network (not restricted to Wi-Fi). Data uploads are configured with an interval of 10 (units in the protocol), and data is not deleted after upload.

Assumptions and questions
- Assumed in the setup: streaming uploads to the CARP backend and that only steps and location data are collected on the smartphone (these align with your stated assumptions).
- There are no open questions listed in the protocol.

In short: the build implements onboarding for a full name, automatic data collection on the phone for steps and hourly location, and streaming data uploads to CARP, using the phone as the primary device.

- Location Task: A background task using the phone’s location service runs every hour. It’s started by the hourly location trigger (Houry Location Trigger, period of 1 hour, starts immediately) and collects location data once per hour.

Onboarding requires the participant’s full name. Data is configured to be uploaded to the backend as a stream, with compression enabled. We assume the location service is a connected service linked to the phone.

Open questions: none identified for this unit. If you want, I can draft a final protocol snippet that shows both tasks and their bindings for review. Next steps: confirm the onboarding field and the backend upload settings match your target CAWS endpoint.

You asked for a setup that continuously watches the phone, adds hourly health data, samples weather and air quality every 30 minutes, and keeps two persistent image-upload tasks, with all data stored on the device and then uploaded to a CARP service. Here’s what’s built, mapped to your requests.

- Passive phone context: The app runs in the background on the participant’s smartphone and quietly collects context data such as steps, location, battery level, screen state, ambient light, user activity, device information, and connectivity (Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth). This runs continuously as a background process on the phone.

- Weather data: Weather information is collected in the background every 30 minutes via a Weather service.

- Air quality data: Air quality information is collected in the background every 30 minutes via an Air Quality service.

- Hourly health data: Every hour, the app collects health-related items including weight, BMI, birth date, gender, steps, heart rate, heart rate variability (RMSSD and SDNN), and all sleep stages. This runs as a background health data task on the smartphone.

- Two image tasks: There are two persistent image capture tasks that stay in the app’s task list:
  - "Upload Best Demo Image" (about 3 minutes to complete)
  - "Upload Best Gadget Image" (about 3 minutes to complete)
  Both are active tasks the participant can do at any time.

- Data destination and flow: All collected data is uploaded to the CARP Web Service. The protocol sets up streaming uploads (data sent in streams), with compression enabled, and an ongoing upload interval specified (unit in the protocol is 10). Data is not deleted from the device after upload.

Assumptions from the plan you approved:
- A single smartphone hosts the data collection app.
- Weather and Air Quality services are available and integrable.
- The hourly health data items listed (weight, BMI, birth date, gender, steps, heart rate, HRV RMSSD/SDNN, sleep stages) are collected as described.
- The two image tasks stay persistent in the app and each takes about 3 minutes.
- All data is stored locally on the device and retained after uploading to the CARP service.

Open questions still to confirm:
- Should birth date and gender be collected only during onboarding or also included as hourly health data? The current setup treats them as hourly health data; please confirm.
- How long should data be kept locally on the device after it’s uploaded? Please specify retention.
- Is streaming data upload acceptable, or should data be stored on upload only? The protocol uses streaming uploads; please confirm.
- Any privacy, anonymization, or data minimization rules to apply to locally stored data before upload? If yes, please specify.

You asked for a setup that quietly collects phone data, adds weather and air quality every 30 minutes, gathers hourly health data, and keeps two image-upload tasks available for participants. Based on the final protocol, here’s what was built and how it matches (and where it diverges) from your intent.

What happens and when
- The app runs in the background on the participant’s smartphone to continuously collect core phone data (steps, location, battery level, screen state, ambient light, activity, device information, and connectivity including Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth). These are treated as ongoing background data collection rather than active tasks for the participant.
- Weather data is collected every 30 minutes via a Weather service, and air quality data is collected every 30 minutes via an Air Quality service.
- Health data is collected hourly. The protocol includes a health data task that records steps, BMI, weight, heart rate, HRV RMSSD and SDNN, and sleep stages; there is also a separate health data task that records only steps.
- A single persistent image upload task named “Image Upload - Best Demo (3 min est)” remains available in the app task list. Participants can complete it by uploading an image and a short description, with an estimated completion time of about 3 minutes. This task is kept available through a trigger that ensures it stays on the task list.

Where data goes and what participants notice
- All collected data are uploaded to a CARP server via a web service, with data being compressed and uploaded in a streaming fashion. Local copies are retained on the device after uploading.
- The primary wearable/phone interaction the participant notices is the persistent image task for the “Best Demo.” The gadget variant described in your intent is not present in the final protocol.

Assumptions and open questions from the plan
- We assumed local copies are kept on the device after upload, weather/air data can run in the background, HRV metrics can come from phone sensors (or wearables), and the image task remains accessible with roughly 3 minutes to complete.

You asked to collect comprehensive mobile health-related metrics continuously, including environmental factors every half hour; additionally capture detailed information from fitness apps and user-generated content tasks periodically. Here is what was built: A study that will actively monitor a smartphone's step count, location tracking capabilities, battery levels, screen activity detection (including when the phone isn't in use), ambient light conditions using its sensors for physical activities recognition by motion data collection; as well as gather detailed system information.

Every half hour during your daily routine and hourly throughout this period, we'll record weather updates from a connected service. The air quality around you will also be assessed at those same intervals to provide insights into the environment you're in regularly — all happening silently without any input required of yours but relying on our smartphone's connectivity capabilities presuming it can transfer data as needed.

Moreover, every hour we’ll peek through your fitness app for specific health metrics such as weight and BMI (though not specified), date-of-birth details to possibly personalize the study insights; various heart rate parameters including a unique index called RMSSD that measures sympathetic nervous system activity which is related to stress responses in you. We'll also check how well you're sleeping by monitoring different sleep stages — like if you've moved from being asleep at night when you'd usually be awake, or vice versa.

Additionally every hour we’ll ask for two images: one where you'll show off a particular skill/task performed as best as possible and another showing any new gadget received since you joined our study. These will help us understand the impact of your activities on health metrics better but won't specify how often to send these requests unless it interferes with privacy or consumes too much battery.

The system assumes that we can keep collecting this data because it's constantly happening in real-time and only stops when you've finished participating, without any further actions needed from you. However, we're still figuring out the best way for all of those tasks — like capturing images on demand as opposed to at set times or automatically every hour; we'll need more research there since it affects how often we ask for data which also impacts your device's resources and battery life.

In summary: a continuous passive monitoring system with an added layer that occasionally checks in through various measures, all happening within the limits of what was assumed about network connectivity but without defining specifics on triggers or timing.
